verses.text: By the LORD's command, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel. Jeroboam was standing by the altar, ready to burn incense.

By the LORD's command, the man of God shouted against the altar, "Altar! Altar! This is what the LORD says: 'A son named Josiah will be born into David's family. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you.'"
That same day he gave a sign. He said, "This is the sign the LORD has given: The altar will split apart, and the ashes on it will spill out."

When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God shouted against the altar in Bethel, he pointed at him from the altar and said, "Grab him!" But the hand he stretched out against the man dried up, so that he could not pull it back.
The altar also split apart, and the ashes spilled out of it, just as the man of God had said in the sign the LORD gave him.

Then the king said to the man of God, "Please ask the LORD your God to be kind to me, and pray for me, so my hand will be healed." So the man of God prayed to the LORD, and the king's hand was healed. It became just as it was before.
The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."
But the man of God answered the king, "Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you. I will not eat bread or drink water in this place.
The LORD commanded me, 'Do not eat bread or drink water, and do not go back the same way you came.'"
So he left by a different road, and did not go back the way he had come to Bethel.
Now an old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him everything the man of God had done there that day. They also told their father what he had said to the king.
Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" His sons had seen which road the man of God from Judah had taken.
He told his sons, "Put a saddle on my donkey." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode off on it.
He went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak tree. He asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He answered, "I am."
Then the prophet said to him, "Come home with me and eat some bread."
The man of God said, "I cannot go back with you or go into your home. I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place.
The LORD told me, 'Do not eat bread or drink water there, and do not go back the same way you came.'"

The old prophet said to him, "I am a prophet too, just like you. An angel gave me a message from the LORD. He said, 'Bring him back to your house so he can eat bread and drink water.'" But he was lying to him.
So the man of God went back with him and ate bread and drank water in his house.
While they were sitting at the table, the LORD's word came to the old prophet who had brought him back.
He shouted to the man of God who had come from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have disobeyed the LORD's word. You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you.
You came back and ate bread and drank water in the place where he told you, "Do not eat bread or drink water." So your body will not be buried in the tomb of your ancestors.'"
When the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet saddled a donkey for him.
As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay on the road, with the donkey standing beside it. The lion stood beside the body too.
Some men passed by and saw the body lying on the road, with the lion standing next to it. They went and told about it in the town where the old prophet lived.

When the old prophet who had brought him back heard about it, he said, "It is the man of God who disobeyed the LORD's word. So the LORD gave him to the lion, and it has torn him and killed him, just as the LORD warned him."
He told his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled it.
He went and found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
The prophet picked up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own town to mourn for him and bury him.
He laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, crying, "Oh, my brother!"
After he buried him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.
What he shouted by the LORD's command against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria will surely come true."
Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil ways. Again he chose priests for the high places from all kinds of people. Anyone who wanted to be a priest, he set apart for the high places.
This sin brought down Jeroboam's family. It led to them being cut off and wiped off the face of the earth.
